# Prince Valiant — RAM-based reinforcement learning

A Windows/Python research project for **The Legend of Prince Valiant (NES)**. It combines a native emulator bridge, RAM observations, demonstration-assisted reinforcement learning, and separate imitation policies for later levels.

## Results

| Level | Selected method | Recorded result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Dueling DQN trained with DQfD | Update 3,000 completed the level in 18,273 native frames; return +108.091791 |
| 2 | Neural behavior cloning | Completion card and subsequent Level 3 entry verified |
| 3 | Raw-RAM neural imitation | Completion card and subsequent Level 4 title verified |

These are known-route results with separate models and reset states. They do not establish the assignment's 7/10 success criterion. Level 1 evaluation from the game's normal start remains unaudited. See [results and evidence](docs/RESULTS.md).

## Getting started

Windows x64, Python 3.13, and NVIDIA CUDA are required by the selected training and gameplay runners. Checkpoints can be inspected on CPU.

```powershell
py -3.13 -m venv .venv
.venv/Scripts/Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pip install -r requirements-cuda.txt
python run.py --list
python run.py inspect_models
```

The repository includes selected checkpoints, logs, code, and videos. ROMs, recordings, training datasets, reset states, and compiled DLLs are not included. Evaluation and training require these additional inputs; see [setup and commands](docs/SETUP.md).

## Documentation

- [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): native bridge, RAM processing, models, and learning code.
- [Results](docs/RESULTS.md): selected checkpoints, measured outcomes, and evidence.
- [Reproducibility](docs/REPRODUCIBILITY.md): verification, required assets, and current limitations.
- [Draft report](docs/case_study_draft/REPORT_DRAFT.pdf): 10-page project report.
- [Progress video](deliverables/videos/progress_presentation.mp4): 4m23.67s presentation; [full-run videos](deliverables/videos/README.md).

Third-party notices and unresolved licensing questions are documented in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). No project-wide license has been selected.

# Setup and commands

Run commands from the repository root. Use a new output directory for every run.

## Python environment

The supported development environment is Windows x64 with CPython 3.13. Selected training and evaluation scripts use CUDA; model inspection uses CPU. Dependency pins reflect the observed environment. A fresh-machine installation has not been verified.

```powershell
py -3.13 -m venv .venv
.venv/Scripts/Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pip install -r requirements-cuda.txt
python run.py --list
python run.py inspect_models
python run.py submission_assets audit
```

## Native emulator and ROM

Install Visual Studio Build Tools with MSVC x64 C++14 support, the Windows SDK, and Visual Studio Installer's `vswhere.exe`. Build the recorder before its ABI2 observer:

```powershell
python instrumentation/build_recorder.py
python instrumentation/build_kind18_observer.py
```

The retained native source has an unresolved licensing provenance issue; see [third-party notices](../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). No compiled binary is included.

Place a legally obtained ROM at `roms/prince_valiant.nes`. Expected SHA-256:

```text
96ad0a41a34fccc98bb7255890b131f77d4131cc69594c77e3ff33cd3a8fe6a5
```

Reset states are bound to the ROM and recorder build identity. Level 1 also checks exact historical DLL and observer-provenance hashes. A fresh build is not verified as compatible with those assets: the original build fingerprint included native tests and benchmarks omitted here. Historical evaluation requires the original compatible assets or a separately validated codec compatibility procedure.

## Required assets

[artifacts.json](../manifests/artifacts.json) records required filenames, sizes, hashes, destinations, and access conditions. Public downloads are not available. The original workspace owner can restore individual local assets:

```powershell
python run.py submission_assets restore --source <research-checkout> --destination <exact-manifest-destination>
```

Restoration rejects existing destinations and hash mismatches. Generating new recordings does not reproduce the selected experiments' pinned identities. Preparation commands can write to fresh locations, but historical consumers still expect their documented destinations and hashes.

## Evaluation

After supplying the required data, states, ROM, and compatible native binaries:

```powershell
python run.py evaluate_selected_level1 --output analysis/submission_l1_eval
python run.py evaluate_level2_confirmed_completion --output analysis/submission_l2_eval
python run.py evaluate_level3_imitation --checkpoint training/level3_imitation_refine_v2_20261026/best.pt --output analysis/submission_l3_eval
python run.py review_level3_imitation --output analysis/submission_l3_eval
```

Level 1 uses the recorded reset-389 protocol. Level 2 checks the completion card and subsequent title. Level 3 independently recomputes every model action and compares ending images against retained references. These commands have been help-checked; no new gameplay was run to verify this repository export.

## Training

### Level 1 DQfD

```powershell
python run.py level1_dqfd_pilot preflight --output training/submission_dqfd
python run.py level1_dqfd_pilot pretrain --output training/submission_dqfd --execution-budget config/submission_execution_budget.json --report-dir analysis/submission_dqfd_receipts --dry-run
```

The execution-budget file is a required future input, not an included artifact. Training requires the pinned demonstration cache, initial actor, and a fresh valid budget/code/protocol chain. Remove `--dry-run` only after those requirements are met. Historical receipts cannot be reused to authorize a new launch. The supported continuation restores Q/target networks, Adam, RNG, and replay priorities from the accepted update-2000 state; arbitrary checkpoint resume and online collection are not exposed by this CLI.

### Level 1 PPO

```powershell
python run.py train_backward_level1 --stage train --config config/backward_level1_v1.json --output training/submission_ppo --updates 1
python run.py train_backward_level1 --stage evaluate --config config/backward_level1_v1.json --output analysis/submission_ppo_eval --resume training/submission_ppo/checkpoints/latest.pt --trials 10 --evaluation-mode greedy
```

This base-config example exercises the retained backward PPO workflow. It is not a reproduction of every historical PPO variant or the selected DQfD result. Route and config-specific normalization/BC inputs are required.

### Levels 2 and 3 imitation

```powershell
python run.py run_level2_title_bc --output training/submission_l2_title --report analysis/submission_l2_title
python run.py train_level3_imitation --output training/submission_l3_initial --steps 20000
python run.py train_level3_imitation --output training/submission_l3_refine --resume training/submission_l3_initial/best.pt --steps 15500 --lr 0.00001
```

Level 2 requires the v56 parent, v4 RAM replay, title preparation, and original recording. Level 3 requires its pinned preparation and demonstration dataset. Its `--resume` option loads actor state and starts a fresh Adam optimizer; it is refinement rather than exact optimizer continuation.

## Data preparation

```powershell
python run.py prepare_backward_level1 --session captures/human/20261013_224343_044974 --output training/submission_route
python run.py prepare_level2_replay --output analysis/submission_l2_replay
python run.py prepare_level2_score_replay --output analysis/submission_l2_score_replay
python run.py prepare_level2_title_bc --output analysis/submission_l2_intro
python run.py prepare_level3_imitation --output analysis/submission_l3_preparation
python run.py prepare_level1_dqfd_transitions --mode preflight --output training/submission_transitions --frame-cap 100000 --artifact-cap-bytes 12884901888 --wall-cap-seconds 1800
```

The DQfD builder's replay mode additionally requires an adapter, fresh resource receipt, and separate lifecycle receipt directory; see `python run.py prepare_level1_dqfd_transitions --help`. Replay and some state-preparation tools execute the emulator. The 100,000-frame preflight example is a bounded parser example, not a validated budget for the complete reconstruction.
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:
# Architecture

## Runtime

The selected workflows use `RecorderNative` to step the NES emulator with raw controller masks and read its 2,048-byte CPU RAM. Full-state snapshots carry ROM, build, and payload identities. Loading a state validates these identities before replacing the native owner.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    ROM[User-supplied ROM] --> Native[Native emulator]
    Native --> RAM[Current RAM]
    RAM --> Encoder[Versioned observation encoder]
    Encoder --> Model[Policy or Q network]
    Model --> Input[Controller mask]
    Input --> Native
    Native --> Evidence[Recorded RAM, actions and images]
    Evidence --> Review[Independent completion review]
    Recording[Branch-aware human recording] --> Dataset[Validated demonstrations]
    Dataset --> Training[Training]
    Training --> Model
```

Human recordings follow checkpoint ancestry across rewinds. Only transitions on the selected ancestry are used; a rewind is not treated as a causal gameplay step.

## Implementation map

| Component | Main implementation |
| --- | --- |
| CLI and paths | `run.py:main`, `paths.py:ROOT` |
| Native ownership and state loading | `recorder_native.py:RecorderNative`, `kind18_observer.py:Kind18ObserverNative` |
| General Gymnasium wrapper | `rl_env.py:PrinceValiantRamEnv` |
| RAM semantics and geometry | `game_state.py`, `scene_state.py`, `navigation.py:NavigationEncoder` |
| Level 1 environment and curriculum | `backward_level1.py:HumanRoute, Level1Env, BackwardCurriculum` |
| Temporal models and history | `training/temporal_models.py`, `training/temporal.py:FrameHistory`, `control_history.py` |
| DQN / DQfD | `training/dqn.py:DuelingQ`, `training/dqfd.py`, `training/dqfd_execution.py` |
| Replay and checkpoint validation | `training/dqfd_transitions.py:TransitionCache`, `training/dqfd_replay.py`, `training/dqfd_pretraining.py:load_committed_milestone` |
| PPO training and workers | `scripts/train_backward_level1.py`, `training/process_envs.py` |
| Level 2 actor and completion check | `training/level2_demonstration_policy.py:DemonstrationActor`, `training/level2_completion_evidence.py:CompletionEvidence` |
| Level 3 actor and ending evidence | `training/level3_imitation.py:Level3ImitationActor`, `training/level3_evidence.py` |

Unqualified modules above are under `src/prince_valiant_rl/`. The [symbol index](../manifests/source_symbols.json) lists exact exported files and their top-level functions/classes. The [dependency graph](../manifests/dependency_graph.json) records transitive imports and dynamic entry points.

## Learning contracts

**Level 1.** The selected checkpoint uses the dueling temporal DQN architecture with 17 actions and 1,234,458 parameters. Its metadata defines feature shapes, categorical/terrain embeddings, CNN/GRU branches, and history offsets `[-60, -30, -15, -9, -6, -3, 0]`. DQfD combines duration-aware one- and ten-step Double-Q targets, demonstration margin supervision, prioritized replay, and the implemented regularizer. The selected continuation is demonstration-only; it performs no online collection. Exact configuration and state hashes are retained in the [selection record](../analysis/level1_dqfd_demo_continuation_20261025/selected_checkpoint.json).

The PPO implementation retains separate policy/value processing, rollout workers, backward suffix curricula, and config-dependent observation/reward variants. Its historical results are not a controlled algorithm comparison with the later DQfD study.

**Level 2.** The selected title-inclusive actor has 559,504 parameters and maps current raw RAM to 16 observed controller masks. Normalization is stored in the checkpoint. Training uses the complete selected human route and a v56 parent actor. The evaluation tail uses ordinary confirm-button inputs after the candidate completion flag; it does not demonstrate learned Level 3 play.

**Level 3.** An independently initialized MLP maps 2,048 current RAM bytes through 512- and 256-unit hidden layers to 22 mask logits, with 1,186,070 parameters. Per-byte normalization follows division by 255, with a 0.02 standard-deviation floor. These are opaque RAM inputs, not verified Level 2 semantics. Inference uses no demonstration lookup, external frame index, or playback cursor.

## Native source

The repository retains only native include/source files, recorder and observer wrappers, build scripts, and notices. Generated trees and DLLs are excluded. See [setup](SETUP.md) for compiler requirements and the historical-state compatibility constraint.
docs/RESULTS.md:
# Results and evidence

All frame counts below are native emulator frames. Recorded outcomes use separate level models and initial states.

## Level 1: selected DQfD checkpoint

| Global optimizer update | Episode frames | Configured return | Terminal |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1,000 | 36,000 | -22.963344 | Time limit |
| 2,000 | 36,000 | -14.202617 | Time limit |
| **3,000** | **18,273** | **108.091791** | **Level completed** |
| 4,000 | 18,273 | 108.091791 | Level completed |
| 5,000 | 27,246 | 6.722021 | Game over |

Updates 3,000 and 4,000 tied; the earlier checkpoint was selected. All continuation updates used the same 21,599 human/policy demonstration transitions and unchanged reward coefficients. Completion cleared objective IDs 513/514/515/516. Update 5,000 regressed; the cause was not established.

Each checkpoint had one greedy episode from reset 389. These outcomes are not a success-rate estimate or a normal-game-start audit.

- [Selected checkpoint and metadata](../analysis/level1_dqfd_demo_continuation_20261025/selected_checkpoint.json)
- [Continuation results](../analysis/level1_dqfd_demo_continuation_20261025/result.json)
- [Earlier 1,000/2,000 study](../analysis/level1_dqfd_extended_study_20261025/result.json)
- [Training metrics](../analysis/level1_dqfd_demo_continuation_20261025/training_metrics.csv) and [source provenance](../manifests/log_provenance.json)
- [Checkpoint outcomes](../analysis/level1_dqfd_demo_continuation_20261025/candidate_comparison.png) and [learning diagnostics](../analysis/level1_dqfd_demo_continuation_20261025/learning_trends.png)

Loss diagnostics use optimizer updates and are not episode-reward curves. Lower fitting loss did not prevent the final checkpoint's regression.

## Level 2: title-inclusive imitation

The selected v57 neural actor controlled 22,509 title/gameplay frames. An extended recording retained the following evidence:

| Event | Frame |
| --- | ---: |
| Candidate flag | 22,509 |
| Visible Level 2 completion card | 22,809 |
| Level 3 title | 23,409 |
| Level 3 gameplay image | 23,709 |

All pre-flag neural actions and post-flag confirm inputs were independently recomputed. Fresh gameplay entry is required before a new completion flag is accepted. The completion card and next-level title corroborate the flag.

The route gained 9,150 game-score points, collected seven E and three T bonuses, and missed ten of twenty observed opportunities. Game score is not a configured episode return. Exact T-counter time units were not inferred.

The title-inclusive route is training data; deterministic replay from the same start is not independent generalization evidence. See [verification](../analysis/level2_transition_tail_v59_20261026/verification.json), [completion card](../analysis/level2_transition_tail_v59_20261026/after_flag_0300.png), and [next-level title](../analysis/level2_transition_tail_v59_20261026/after_flag_0900.png).

## Level 3: raw-RAM imitation

The 49,100-row selected-ancestry dataset was used entirely for training. The initial 20,000-update fit matched 49,036 source actions; 15,500 further low-rate hard-example updates reached 49,100/49,100 agreement in the single-row runtime inference path. This is training agreement, not held-out accuracy.

The reviewed run retained 49,775 model decisions. The completion card appeared at frame 47,975 and the Level 4 title at 49,175. Every action was independently recomputed. The first 49,100 source-range RAM frames matched the reference; the 675-frame transition tail is not evidence of broad generalization.

There were no mid-run resets, RAM interventions, reference-action substitutions, or optimizer updates. The title comparison permits exact image matching within a bounded vertical scroll offset. Reaching the Level 4 title does not establish Level 4 competence.

See [verification](../analysis/level3_imitation_evaluation_v2_20261026/verification.json), [completion card](../analysis/level3_imitation_evaluation_v2_20261026/frame_047975.png), [Level 4 title](../analysis/level3_imitation_evaluation_v2_20261026/frame_049175.png), and the [initial](../training/level3_imitation_v1_20261026/fit.jsonl) and [refined](../training/level3_imitation_refine_v2_20261026/fit.jsonl) fitting logs.

## Scope

The assignment requires at least seven successful episodes out of ten for each level, with Level 1 starting from the game's normal start. Those criteria remain unestablished. Levels 2 and 3 use imitation learning; the selected Level 1 continuation uses demonstration-assisted TD learning without online interaction. Controlled diagnostic probes are separate from normal-input gameplay evaluation.

# Reproducibility and verification

## Included artifacts

The repository contains environment, training, evaluation and preparation code; three selected checkpoints; authentic selected metrics; a 10-page draft report; and four videos.

| Model | Checkpoint |
| --- | --- |
| Level 1 DQfD, update 3,000 | `training/level1_dqfd_demo_continuation_20261025/checkpoint_3000.pt` |
| Level 2 title-inclusive imitation | `training/level2_title_bc_v57_20261026/actor.pt` |
| Level 3 refined imitation | `training/level3_imitation_refine_v2_20261026/best.pt` |

[Artifact records](../manifests/artifacts.json) contain SHA-256 hashes, byte sizes, access conditions, and destinations. The Level 1 committed receipt preserves model/optimizer/replay/RNG identities. Levels 2 and 3 include normalization buffers and action vocabularies in their checkpoints.

Recorded seeds are 20261024 for selected DQfD training, 20261128 for Level 2 fitting, and 20261130 for Level 3 fitting. The base PPO config uses 20261015; the selected Level 1 lineage config uses 20261022. These apply to their respective experiments, not a single shared run.

## Verification performed

[verification.json](../manifests/verification.json) records:

- Compilation checks and help checks for all 16 advertised CLI commands.
- Isolated Python imports resolved from this repository.
- CPU checkpoint hash, schema, and state-shape validation.
- Selected Level 1 configuration hash validation.
- Video hashes/metadata and the report's 10-page count.
- Source-copy hash comparisons and exclusion/path checks performed during preparation.

The checks used the existing Windows environment. A fresh-machine installation, native compilation/loading, new emulator evaluation, and training were not performed. Runtime code and selected models were unchanged by the documentation cleanup.

## Reproduction requirements

Gameplay and training require a legally obtained ROM, compatible native binaries, and the pinned reset/data artifacts. These inputs are not included or publicly hosted. The original owner can restore exact local inputs using the hash-checked asset tool; see [setup](SETUP.md).

Checkpoint loading is verified. End-to-end evaluation and training are not ready from a public clone alone. New DQfD training additionally requires a fresh valid budget/code/protocol chain. A newly compiled native source tree has a different fingerprint from the historical tree; selected-state compatibility needs separate validation.

## Scientific and submission limits

- Known-route clears do not establish seven successful episodes out of ten.
- Level 1 normal-start compliance remains unaudited.
- Imitation agreement on the training route is not held-out accuracy.
- Episode reward telemetry is unavailable for the selected Level 2/3 videos.
- The report is a draft; a revised LaTeX report is not included.
- The short video uses accelerated playback and separate resets/models; acceptance of that presentation format is unresolved.
- The repository is public at the owner's request; the assignment originally specified private access.
- Native-source licensing provenance and project-wide licensing remain unresolved.

## Source and export records

[provenance.json](../manifests/provenance.json) records original/exported hashes; [inventory.json](../manifests/inventory.json) describes current files. [dependency_graph.json](../manifests/dependency_graph.json) and [source_symbols.json](../manifests/source_symbols.json) support implementation review.

Tests, fixtures, private recordings, ROMs, reset states, generated builds, virtual environments, and unrelated research tooling are excluded. The original research workspace preserves them.

To rebuild an export from the original workspace into a new directory:

```powershell
python packaging/prepare_export.py --source <research-checkout> --output <new-empty-path>
```

The exporter refuses an existing destination, follows selected dependency closures, and performs static/help/model checks. It does not launch training or emulator gameplay.

# Gameplay videos

Start with [progress_presentation.mp4](progress_presentation.mp4): **4m23.67s**, 1280×960, 30 FPS, H.264. It shows early and middle Level 1 DQfD checkpoints followed by the selected Level 1–3 runs.

| Video | Duration | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Presentation](progress_presentation.mp4) | 263.67 s | Early/middle at 24×; selected runs at 8× |
| [Level 1](level1_full_run_1x.mp4) | 304.60 s | Selected DQfD update 3,000, real time |
| [Level 2](level2_full_run_1x.mp4) | 415.17 s | Neural imitation through completion and Level 3 entry |
| [Level 3](level3_full_run_1x.mp4) | 829.60 s | Neural imitation through completion and Level 4 title |

Each source run is continuous; presentation cuts occur between runs and title cards. Gameplay retains its original aspect ratio, with labels outside the game image. No game audio or voiceover was available.

The levels use separate models and initial states. This is not one uninterrupted three-level game. Level 1 shows the recorded episode return; Levels 2 and 3 show reward as N/A because configured episode-return telemetry is unavailable. Level 2 game score is labelled separately.

The brief requests a 3–5-minute presentation and full runs. These runs total about 26 minutes at real time, so the presentation uses labelled acceleration and includes real-time companions. Whether that satisfies the brief's intended format remains unresolved.

[manifest.original.json](manifest.original.json) records output hashes, source identities, durations, frame rates, and playback speeds. Current output hashes were verified during repository preparation. [Results](../../docs/RESULTS.md) explains the scientific scope.

# prince_valiant_rl

Reusable environment and observation code: native ownership/state loading, RAM semantics, scene geometry, navigation encoding, controller history, and Level 1 reset/curriculum logic.

[training/](training/) contains reusable models and learning components. Experiment outputs live separately in the repository-root `training/` directory. Native execution requires the assets described in [setup](../../docs/SETUP.md).
src/prince_valiant_rl/training/README.md:
# Learning components

Reusable temporal models, replay stores, losses, process workers, checkpoint validation, and level-specific imitation actors.

- `dqfd*.py` and `dqn.py`: demonstration-assisted Double-Q learning, prioritized replay, supervision, and strict state restoration.
- `temporal*.py`, `process_envs.py`, and `window_storage.py`: history encoding and batched training support.
- `level2_demonstration_policy.py` and `level3_imitation.py`: the selected raw-RAM imitation actors.

These are implementation modules. Trained weights and logs are in the repository-root [training directory](../../../training/). See [architecture](../../../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) for model contracts.

python packaging/prepare_export.py --source <research-checkout> --output <new-empty-path>

[videos/](videos/) contains the progress presentation and three real-time level-run companions, with metadata and scope notes.

The [draft PDF report](../docs/case_study_draft/REPORT_DRAFT.pdf) and its editable source/assets are under `docs/case_study_draft/`. Selected models and fitting logs are under [training/](../training/).
docs/case_study_draft/README.md:
# Draft project report

[REPORT_DRAFT.pdf](REPORT_DRAFT.pdf) is the 10-page draft report. [REPORT_DRAFT.md](REPORT_DRAFT.md) is its editable text, and [assets/](assets/) contains figures, plotted data, and source provenance.

The draft predates the final repository presentation and is not the requested revised LaTeX report. For the current selected-model identities, evidence, and reproduction constraints, consult [results](../RESULTS.md) and [reproducibility](../REPRODUCIBILITY.md).
analysis/level1_dqfd_demo_continuation_2:
# Level 1 DQfD continuation

`selected_checkpoint.json` identifies update 3,000. `result.json` and `verification.json` record the completed continuation; `training_metrics.csv` contains 3,000 extracted optimizer-update diagnostics. PNGs summarize learning and recorded checkpoint outcomes.

One greedy reset-389 episode per checkpoint; no 7/10 campaign or normal-start audit.

See [results and interpretation](../../docs/RESULTS.md) and [full-run videos](../../deliverables/videos/README.md).
analysis/level1_dqfd_extended_study_2026:
# Level 1 early DQfD milestones

Results and figures for the update-1,000 and update-2,000 demonstration-only study, before the successful continuation.

Both recorded milestone episodes timed out. Lower fitting loss did not establish completion.

See [results and interpretation](../../docs/RESULTS.md) and [full-run videos](../../deliverables/videos/README.md).

analysis/level2_transition_tail_v59_2026:
# Level 2 completion corroboration

`verification.json` records the independently checked actions and bonus ledger. Screenshots retain the completion card at frame 22,809 and Level 3 title at frame 23,409.

The actor controls the title/gameplay segment; ordinary confirm inputs advance post-clear screens. This is a known-route imitation result.

See [results and interpretation](../../docs/RESULTS.md) and [full-run videos](../../deliverables/videos/README.md).
analysis/level3_imitation_evaluation_v2_:
# Level 3 reviewed evaluation

`verification.json` records all-action recomputation and terminal-reference checks. Completion is visible at frame 47,975 and the Level 4 title at frame 49,175.

All 49,100 source rows were training data. The Level 4 title is not evidence of Level 4 competence.

See [results and interpretation](../../docs/RESULTS.md) and [full-run videos](../../deliverables/videos/README.md).
